html:
The Kisêdjê, also known as the Suyá, are a Jê people of the upper Xingu River in Mato Grosso, Brazil.

They were known for lip discs: after marriage men pierced the lower lip and wore a wooden disc in it. They came to the upper Xingu in the 1800s and took up some ways of the older Xingu peoples such as the Kamayurá and the Kalapalo. Wars with the Kayapó and the Ikpeng cut their numbers.

The Villas-Bôas brothers contacted them in 1959, and they came under the protection of the Xingu Indigenous Park, created in 1961. The anthropologist Anthony Seeger wrote about their music in "Why Suyá Sing".
sum: The Kisêdjê, also known as the Suyá, are a Jê people of the upper Xingu River in Mato Grosso, Brazil.
